problem.question: Chad sandwiches 2 crackers with a scoop of peanut butter.  He has 5 of these crackers a night before bed.  A box of crackers has 4 sleeves with each sleeve holding 28 crackers.  How many nights will 5 boxes of crackers last him?
problem.answer:
Chad uses 2 crackers for each "sandwich" and has 5 sandwiches a night so he eats 2*5 = <<2*5=10>>10 crackers a night
The box has 4 sleeves of crackers and each sleeve has 28 crackers for a total of 4*28 = <<4*28=112>>112 crackers
1 box has 112 crackers so 5 boxes will have 112*5 = <<112*5=560>>560 crackers
He eats 10 crackers a night and 5 boxes have 560 crackers so they will last him 560//10 = <<560//10=56>>56 nights
#### 56

generation.text:
He has 5 boxes of crackers and each box has 4 sleeves so he has 5*4 = 20 sleeves of crackers
Each sleeve has 28 crackers and he has 20 sleeves so he has 28*20 = 560 crackers
He has 560 crackers and he uses 2 at a time so he can eat 560/2 = 280 crackers
He eats 280 crackers a night and he has 5 nights so he will last 280*5 = 1400 nights
The final answer is \boxed{1400}.
